title: Linux 7.3-rc2 Released Following Another Busy Week
summary: Linux 7.3-rc2 release candidate marks progress toward stable v7.3 kernel with active development cycle ongoing. For 5G RAN embedded developers, this release cycle introduces potential driver updates, networking stack improvements, and real-time performance enhancements critical for DU/CU workload optimization. Key focus: early testing of rc2 is essential to identify stability issues before production deployment in communication infrastructure.

title: [$] Fixing the TCMalloc regression with RSEQ operations
summary: This article addresses a kernel regression in restartable sequences (RSEQ) that broke TCMalloc memory allocator in Linux 6.19, where user-space lockless operations relied on undocumented kernel behavior. For embedded/5G firmware developers, this highlights critical compatibility issues between kernel optimization changes and memory management in real-time systems, requiring careful validation of RSEQ-dependent code in high-performance RAN applications.

summary: A new x86 implementation from a non-Intel/AMD entity introduces Advanced Performance Extensions (APX), FRED, and x86S features that exceed current Intel Xeon capabilities with enhanced AMX tile configurations. While this targets general computing, it signals architectural evolution that could influence future embedded x86-based RAN infrastructure, particularly for signal processing acceleration and matrix operations critical to 5G baseband processing.

title: YuzukiNeko – A Linux-capable Allwinner F101 RISC-V SBC with Raspberry Pi Pico form factor
summary: YuzukiNeko introduces a Pico-sized RISC-V SBC featuring Allwinner's F101 SoC with C907 core, MIPI DSI/LVDS display support, and GPIO headers for Linux deployment. For embedded 5G engineers, this represents a practical, low-cost RISC-V platform for prototyping edge RAN processing, sensor integration, and network function virtualization in compact form factors, though performance constraints require validation for real-time workloads.
raw_snippet: YuzukiHD has made another open-source hardware Linux SBC. YuzukiNeko is a Raspberry Pi Pico-sized single board computer powered by a new Allwinner F101 RISC-V SoC. The Allwinner F101 processor features a single 1.008 GHz C907 RISC-V core, 8MB or 16 MB PSRAM, and support for various display interfaces such as MIPI DSI, 24-bit RGB, and LVDS. title: Budgeting Bytes: A Windowed Storage Roofline and Dual-Budget Architecture Ablations for Storage-Bound LLM Decoding
summary: This paper analyzes autoregressive LLM decoding on low-cost hardware by focusing on the bytes-per-token memory bandwidth bottleneck. It introduces a windowed storage roofline model and dual-budget architectures to optimize data movement across memory hierarchies.

title: MonoMoE: An Efficient Fused Mega-kernel for Quantized MoE Decoding
summary: MonoMoE is proposed as an efficient fused mega-kernel designed to optimize quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoding. It addresses computation inefficiencies in sparse expert execution by eliminating token-major tiling overheads.

summary: This paper presents a Hardware-Conscious Software Training (HCST) method to counter DNN inference accuracy loss caused by manufacturing variations in accelerator chips. The approach allows hardware-level variabilities to be mitigated during the software training phase.

title: Network Availability Enhancement in Low-Altitude HetNets: A Cross-Layer Design Perspective
summary: This paper proposes computing-communication resource interchange methods to enhance network availability in low-altitude heterogeneous networks by addressing communication conflicts, extreme heterogeneity, and mixed delays. For 5G RAN firmware engineers, this cross-layer design approach is directly applicable to improving reliability in dense small-cell deployments, UAV-integrated networks, and non-terrestrial RAN scenarios with dynamic resource constraints.

title: Tuning Collective Patterns to Alleviate Congestion in Shared AI Clusters
summary: This study investigates tuning collective communication patterns to mitigate network congestion in shared AI clusters during distributed training. This client-side approach offers an alternative to global workload scheduling or specialized hardware-based routing.

title: Waves on the Walls: Empirical Characterization of mmWave Lateral Waves for Enhanced Indoor Coverage
summary: This work empirically characterizes lateral wave propagation along building interfaces for mmWave coverage extension, introducing a paradigm shift from traditional obstacle-avoidance beamforming strategies. For 5G RAN firmware developers, this provides novel channel modeling insights essential for optimizing indoor mmWave beamforming algorithms, antenna array tuning, and coverage enhancement in FR2 bands without relying on conventional line-of-sight propagation assumptions.

title: Adaptive Context Parallelism for Production LLM Serving
summary: The authors introduce an adaptive context parallelism framework designed to optimize LLM serving for long-context requests. The system dynamically scales the parallelism degree to match varying memory and computational workloads in production.

title: Why faster coding isn't making delivery any faster
summary: While generative AI significantly accelerates individual code writing, it does not necessarily translate to faster software delivery cycles. The bottleneck often shifts to code integration, testing, and verifying the overall quality of AI-generated code.
raw_snippet: Generative AI promised to eliminate one of the biggest sources of friction in software engineering: Writing code. In many ways, it has delivered. Today, an AI coding agent can implement features in minutes that might have taken an engineer an hour. It can generate tests, refactor code, write documentation, navigate large repositories, and even execute development tasks autonomously.
